title: Power and Talent Biggest AI Bottlenecks, Say Data Center Firms
source_used: Yahoo Finance copy of Bloomberg (The Next Web read as well)
key_facts: Executives from some of the largest data center companies said at Bloomberg's New Economy Forum in New Delhi on Tuesday (13 Oct 2026) that access to energy and skilled labor are the two key constraints on the AI data center build-out.
Abhijit Dubey, chief executive of NTT Data, called talent the hidden bottleneck, saying an electrician in the US now earns about $200,000.
Sourcing the correct equipment can take as long as 42 weeks, Dubey said; he also said 'capital is not an issue'.
Connor Teskey, chief executive of Brookfield Asset Management, said demand will outstrip supply through the end of the decade and beyond.
Teskey said Brookfield is 'incredibly selective' and argued the build-out differs from circular AI deals because most is backed by long take-or-pay contracts with strong corporate customers.
Salil Parekh, chief executive of Indian outsourcing firm Infosys, named backlash against the build-out in Western markets as a risk.
Bloomberg News has reported that powering up a data center can now cost as much as $3 billion in the US.
quote_evidence: The data center buildout is barely keeping up with AI development, with access to energy and skilled labor the two key constraints, according to executives from some of the largest companies in the sector.
Demand will outstrip supply through the end of this decade and beyond, said Connor Teskey, CEO of Brookfield Asset Management, one of the world's biggest commercial real estate landlords.
Still, "capital is not an issue," said Dubey.
why_it_matters_hint: Industry leaders say the limit on AI building is now electricity and skilled workers rather than chips or money.
notes: Bloomberg original blocked (bot check); Bloomberg text read on Yahoo Finance and cross-read in The Next Web. Views are from executives with a business interest.
